focus: E2: six-file hub version carriers, parity rules 13a-13d, changelog allocation and the parallel-branch number collision
noveltyJustification: All 9 findings are new to this research; one reuses the packet's own problem statement as the collision evidence.
answeredQuestions: Q2: E2 - What is the root cause of the six-file hub version bump plus changelog collision and the smallest fix that removes the multi-file bump requirement?
ruledOut: derive follower versions at read time
standalone bump script as primary fix

label: The parity contract is explicit across five rules: SKILL.md is authority; ROUTER.md/description.json/hub-router.json/mode-registry.json must equal it (13a); newest changelog entry equals it (13b); README should (13c); packet SKILL.md matches its newest changelog entry (13d).
Live sk-doc state: 13a PASS, 13b PASS, 13d PASS (14 packets), 13c WARN — README 2.2.0.77 vs SKILL.md 2.3.0.0.
README drift is tolerated on exactly the four hubs that have it: README_VERSION_WARN_ONLY = cli-classifier, cli-external-orchestration, sk-doc, system-deep-loop.
The changelog command allocates next_version from the local checkout's changelog list and resolves collisions by incrementing BUILD locally; it writes only the changelog file, never the six carriers.
Author guidance names one field ('Update frontmatter version field') while six files plus a changelog filename must move together.
No commit-time version parity check exists; the pre-commit gates do not run 13a-13d, so a bumped-but-mismatched hub lands before any check reads it.
The packet's own problem statement records the merge collision of a changelog number as an experienced 092-epic failure.

Root cause: version is a hand-allocated, multiply-stored value with no single writer; the only allocator sees one checkout and writes one file, the carriers are hand-bumped from guidance naming one, and parity is doctor-time with a warn carve-out for README.

Smallest fix: empty the README warn set (value change), then extend /create:changelog to allocate against the shared ref and write all six carriers plus the changelog in one command; keep the parity check as a commit-time safety net; registry/lock and standalone scripts fail the reversal-cost order.
